# zdotc

> Forms the dot product of two complex vectors ZDOTC = Xᴴ·Y.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zdotc from '@rreusser/blahpack/blas/base/zdotc';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zdotc( N, x, strideX, y, strideY ) → Complex128
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of complex elements |
| `x` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Input array |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | `x` stride length |
| `y` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Input array |
| ↳ `strideY` | `integer` | `y` stride length |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: number of elements in input vector(s)

</details>

**Returns** `Complex128`: conjugate dot product

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zdotc.ndarray( N, x, strideX, offsetX, y, strideY, offsetY ) → Complex128
```

Forms the dot product of two complex vectors ZDOTC = Xᴴ·Y, using alternative indexing semantics.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of complex elements |
| `x` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | First complex input vector |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | Stride for `x` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetX` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `x` (in complex elements) |
| `y` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Second complex input vector |
| ↳ `strideY` | `integer` | Stride for `y` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetY` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `y` (in complex elements) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: number of elements in input vector(s)

</details>

**Returns** `Complex128`: conjugate dot product

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument must be a nonnegative integer

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `zdotc()` corresponds to the reference BLAS routine [`ZDOTC`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/BLAS/SRC/zdotc.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import zdotc from '@rreusser/blahpack/blas/base/zdotc';

// Compute conjugate dot product of complex vectors:
const x = new Complex128Array( [ 1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0 ] );
const y = new Complex128Array( [ 1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0 ] );

// Using the standard interface:
let result = zdotc( 2, x, 1, y, 1 );
console.log( result ); // eslint-disable-line no-console

// Using the ndarray interface:
result = zdotc.ndarray( 2, x, 1, 0, y, 1, 0 );
console.log( result ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference BLAS 3.12.0 source of `ZDOTC`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZDOTC forms the dot product of two complex vectors

$$
\mathrm{ZDOTC} = X^H \, Y
$$

### Further Details

jack dongarra, 3/11/78. modified 12/3/93, array(1) declarations changed to array(\*)

</section>
